nodes.conceptSummary:
### 1. Pangkal Anomali
Selama ini kita memproses informasi dengan saklar biner yang bernilai mutlak 0 atau 1. Cara ini bekerja sangat baik sampai kita menghadapi persoalan pencarian ruang kombinasi besar di mana cara sekuensial membutuhkan waktu lebih lama dari usia alam semesta. Saklar klasik tidak mampu merepresentasikan ruang kemungkinan paralel tanpa menduplikasi sirkuit fisik secara masif.

### 2. Prototipe Intuitif
Bayangkan alih-alih saklar lampu on/off yang kaku, kita memiliki koin logam di atas meja. Ketika koin diam terlentang di sisi '0', ia adalah bit klasik. Namun, sistem kita memiliki **Tuas Penyeimbang (dikenal sebagai Gerbang Hadamard)**. Ketika tuas Hadamard ini disentak, koin diputar kencang di atas meja. Selama koin berputar seimbang, statusnya bukan angka mutlak dan bukan gambar mutlak, melainkan kombinasi dinamis di mana kedua sisi memiliki potensi muncul yang setara saat dihentikan.

contrastingCases.beginnerMisconception: Qubit menyimpan nilai 0 dan 1 sekaligus saat dibaca di layar.
contrastingCases.physicalReality: Qubit hanya berada dalam superposisi saat terisolasi. Pengukuran memaksanya runtuh menjadi salah satu nilai pasti.

contrastingCases.beginnerMisconception: Pengukuran bersifat pasif dan tidak mengubah sistem.
contrastingCases.physicalReality: Pengukuran adalah operasi fisik aktif yang menghancurkan superposisi.

contrastingCases.beginnerMisconception: Gerbang Hadamard mengubah koin menjadi bit acak rusak.
contrastingCases.physicalReality: Hadamard adalah operasi rotasi deterministik yang presisi menciptakan superposisi seimbang.

forwardPass.microPrimer: "A classical bit is strictly either 0 or 1. A qubit is a quantum system that can exist in a simultaneous linear superposition of |0> and |1>. A Hadamard gate is a foundational quantum operation that transforms a definite state |0> into an equal superposition where both outcomes become equally likely upon measurement."

forwardPass.prompt: "If a qubit initialized in state |0> is transformed by a Hadamard gate into an equal superposition, predict the probability distribution of measuring |0> versus |1>."

options.text: Equal 50% probability for |0> and 50% probability for |1>, because the Hadamard gate creates an equal superposition (|0> + |1>)/sqrt(2), and measuring collapses the probability proportional to squared amplitude |1/sqrt(2)|^2 = 0.5.
options.causalRationale: Correct! The Hadamard gate generates an equal linear superposition where amplitudes are 1/sqrt(2). Squaring the amplitude yields 0.5 for each basis state.

options.text: 100% probability for |0> and 0% for |1>, because an isolated bit cannot change its underlying binary value without an external classical flip operation.
options.causalRationale: Classical Fallacy: Treats qubits as classical deterministic bits. Qubits obey linear quantum superposition, not classical binary states.
options.specificRemediation: Review Prerequisite: Understand that qubits exist in linear superposition prior to measurement.

options.text: 70.7% probability for |0> and 70.7% probability for |1>, because the wave function amplitude 1/sqrt(2) translates directly into measurement probability without squaring.
options.causalRationale: Amplitude Squaring Slip: Confuses state amplitude (1/sqrt(2) approx 0.707) with Born rule measurement probability (|amplitude|^2).
options.specificRemediation: Born Rule Invariant: Measurement probabilities are given by the absolute square of the amplitude |alpha|^2, not the raw amplitude.

options.text: The qubit simultaneously outputs both 0 and 1 in reality, so measuring it records both states at the exact same physical moment.
options.causalRationale: Collapse Misconception: Measurement strictly collapses the superposition into a single definite classical outcome (|0> OR |1>), never both simultaneously.
options.specificRemediation: Measurement Invariant: Measurement forces a quantum collapse into exactly one eigenvalue state.

forwardPass.groundTruth: "Measurement collapses the equal superposition (1/sqrt(2)|0> + 1/sqrt(2)|1>) into |0> with 50% probability and |1> with 50% probability."
